summary.text: A 43-year-old woman with a history of pulmonary embolism diagnosed 5 years earlier, managed with apixaban but with poor adherence, presented with 2 h of central chest pain and breathlessness. She had no cardiac risk factors. On arrival she was profoundly hypotensive at 60/30 mmHg and tachycardic at 115 b.p.m., with a parasternal heave and clear lung fields.

The electrocardiogram showed inferior ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF, and the arterial blood gas showed acute Type I respiratory failure with an arterial oxygen pressure of 5.5 kPa. Coronary angiography showed complete occlusion of the right coronary artery by a large thrombus with a normal left system, and a concurrent acute pulmonary embolism was suspected.

Intracoronary tPA was given and thrombus aspiration obtained three large clots, establishing TIMI III flow with blood pressure improving to a systolic 100 mmHg. CT pulmonary angiography confirmed acute pulmonary embolism, and the full tPA protocol was completed intravenously. Echocardiography with bubble saline revealed a patent foramen ovale and a dilated right ventricle, and right heart catheterization at 2 months showed a mean pulmonary arterial pressure of 33 mmHg.

Pulmonary endarterectomy, with pulmonary pressure reduced from 47 mmHg to 18 mmHg, and PFO closure were performed 6 months after the index presentation. At 12 months of follow-up she was symptomatically well with marked improvement, and her 6-min walk distance had improved from 80 m to 411 m. The authors concluded that the myocardial infarction was caused by paradoxical emboli.
